diagnosis.narrative: The series is dominated by a strong upward trend (a net rise of ~36% of its level). Seasonality is strong (period 52): a repeating cycle explains much of the movement. Predictability is middling — structured signal and irregular noise are balanced. The series reads as ambiguous by the ADF/KPSS tests. A few outliers stand out (1 points, ~1% of the sample). Across validation windows the model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau -0.146), which favours a robust combination.

test a different weighting scheme (softmax_neg_error) to see if a more extreme weighting improves over inverse_error, given unstable ranking and correlated errors.
The series has strong trend/seasonality but ranking is unstable; a trimmed mean may reduce influence of outlier models.
Test a robust non‑weighted average – median – to see if a simple central tendency improves over trimmed mean on this strongly seasonal, highly outlier‑laden series.
The series has strong trend and seasonality but ranking is unstable; a simple mean might capture diverse patterns without overfitting to a few models.
ranking is unstable and several models have correlated errors; a forward‑selection weighted combo may pick a complementary subset.
The series has unstable ranking and many correlated errors; a robust DBA may outperform simple weighted means.
softmax gives more emphasis to the best models while still using a robust pool.
Test a weighted combo on the correlated‑stable pool4 using inverse_error weights to see if a simpler weighting improves over the DBA leader.
test a per‑horizon weighted combo (best_per_horizon) on the full pool to exploit horizon‑varying best models given unstable ranking.

decision.justification: Selected 'dba' (an agent proposal) as the best of 11 backtested attempts, score 0.9603. Series context: trend strength 1.0 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.146); 6 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 1.419.
